question: Why can material wealth never equal the value of the Kaula teaching?
premises: An ocean filled with jewels is imagined
Even this is implied to be incomparable to the teaching
inference: Even possession of an ocean full of jewels cannot match the value of this teaching.
uncertainties: The fused form akretuṃ is difficult and may be a textual corruption.
plain_english: Even if one possessed an ocean filled with jewels, it would not be enough.
